note: Material properties for the rows McMaster labels "Spring Steel" are taken as music wire (ASTM A228). First inferred from McMaster's own published max loads -- assuming hard-drawn A227 puts 513 of 1,523 springs above allowable stress at their own rating, music wire leaves 25 -- and since confirmed on the McMaster product page for 9657K79, which states "Steel Grade: Music-Wire Steel". The 56 springs in the 96485K series are the exception: their product pages name no steel grade, rate to 300 F where music wire and hard-drawn reach only 250 F, and run to 0.625 in wire, far beyond the range music wire is drawn in. They are taken as oil-tempered A229, the 300 F grade. Shear modulus is identical for all these grades, so rate, coil count and solid length never depend on any of it; only stress does.
